title: Routine lane: no claim, lease, anchor, or window for routine changes
objective: Keep the Task Hall's checkpoint, claim, lease, anchor, and continuation machinery for coordinated, evidence-bearing, or rule-changing work, and let routine changes (documentation, tests, tooling, non-breaking package changes) enter through the start-here path with the merge-readiness verdict as the only gate.
current_question: Does exempting routine changes from the checkpoint machinery lose any accountability the repository needs, given that every routine change still carries an accountable GitHub identity, a changelog entry, the repository contract, and the verdict?

assumptions.statement: The maintainer and their Agent needed five round trips to land a routine change; an outside contributor faces the same cost plus the reading load of the Task Hall, which is a barrier the contribution route was not meant to be.
The rule took effect on 2026-09-16 by maintainer direction under the prototype principle of acting and keeping the undo; the introducing commit named in CHANGELOG.md is the undo.

options.summary: Routine changes skip claims, leases, anchors, continuation receipts, and windows; the verdict, changelog discipline, and a named identity are the accountability.
trade_offs: Ten-minute path for people and Agents
Two routine changes can collide on the same file; git and the verdict's conflict check resolve it after the fact instead of a lease preventing it

options.summary: Keep the claim and lease requirement for every change.
trade_offs: Keeps the entry fee that stopped the maintainer's own contributions

agreements: Non-routine work keeps the full checkpoint machinery under both options.
disagreements: Whether reservation is worth its cost for small changes is the open question.
missing_evidence: One outside contributor completing the start-here path end to end.

non_goals: No change to claims, leases, or continuation receipts for non-routine work.
execution.exact_next_action: Until 2026-09-23T14:00:00Z anyone may add a risk or counterexample delta. If none exists when the window closes, the weekly steward records OPT-ROUTINE-LANE by lazy consensus with decided_by process:mandate.weekly-steward.v1; an objection keeps the record with a person and the maintainer reverts the introducing commit if it holds.

reopen_conditions: Two routine changes collide in a way the verdict did not catch before merge.
